    This is an estimate for planning. It covers federal income tax, FICA, and simplified state income tax. It does not include local or paid-leave taxes. Your employer's payroll system may calculate a different amount.

    How does Alabama tax a paycheck?

    Alabama taxes wage income on a graduated schedule with only three brackets. For a single filer, a head of family, or a married person filing separately, the first $500 of taxable income is taxed at 2%, the next $2,500 at 4%, and everything above $3,000 at 5%. A married couple filing jointly gets the same rates on wider bands: 2% on the first $1,000, 4% on the next $5,000, and 5% above $6,000. The 5% top rate is one of the lowest ceilings among the states that tax wages, and the Code of Alabama sets these rates in § 40-18-5.

    Two features separate Alabama from most states. First, Alabama allows a deduction for the federal income tax a taxpayer paid, so the state does not simply start from federal taxable income. Second, Alabama grants a personal exemption of $1,500 for a single filer, a married person filing separately, or a head of family, and $3,000 for a married couple filing jointly. The 2026 data behind this calculator applies a $3,000 single-filer standard deduction to stand in for those adjustments, so the state line here is an estimate rather than the figure an employer withholds.

    Alabama levies no local or county income tax on wages. A handful of the larger cities, including Birmingham, Montgomery, and Gadsden, charge a municipal occupational tax of about 1% or less under their own ordinances, and this calculator does not model it, so a worker inside one of those city limits nets slightly less. The state also runs no disability insurance fund and no paid family leave payroll tax, so no state leave benefit is withheld.

    How Alabama take-home pay is calculated

    1. Gross pay per period. Take your yearly salary, or an hourly rate multiplied by hours worked, and express it as one paycheck for your pay frequency.
    2. Pre-tax deductions first. A traditional 401(k), an HSA, or a health premium lowers the wages that federal and Alabama income tax are charged on.
    3. Federal income tax. The federal standard deduction is removed, then the remaining income runs up the federal marginal brackets.
    4. FICA. Social Security at 6.2% up to the annual wage base, Medicare at 1.45%, and the extra 0.9% Medicare tax above the high-earner threshold.
    5. Alabama income tax. Alabama subtracts its standard deduction and then applies the 2%, 4%, and 5% brackets, so only the dollars above $3,000 of single-filer taxable income reach the top rate.
    6. Model caveat. This calculator applies the dataset's simplified $3,000 single-filer standard deduction and does not subtract the federal income tax deduction Alabama allows, so the state line runs somewhat high; a city occupational tax would reduce take-home pay further.

    The result is your net pay for the period you selected. Pay frequency matters: a biweekly schedule pays 26 times a year and a semi-monthly schedule 24, so the same salary produces different per-paycheck amounts.

    Worked example: $55,000 in Alabama

    A single filer earning $55,000 a year, paid bi-weekly in 2026:

    LinePer paycheck
    Gross pay$2,115.38
    Federal income tax$170.00
    Social Security$131.15
    Medicare$30.67
    Alabama state income tax$61.35
    Net take-home pay$1,722.21

    That is $44,777.50 a year, an effective tax rate of about 18.6%. Change the inputs in the calculator above to see your own numbers.

    How Alabama compares

    Alabama's 5% top rate is low by national standards. It sits above the flat rates in Georgia (4.99%) and North Carolina (3.99%), and far below the top marginal rates in California, New Jersey, or New York. Because Alabama has no state or county income tax on wages, the state bracket is usually the only income-tax line on an Alabama paycheck, unlike Ohio or Pennsylvania, where a municipal or school district rate is withheld on top.

    Alabama runs no state disability insurance and no paid family leave payroll tax, so there is no state leave deduction the way there is in California, New Jersey, Washington, or Minnesota. Alabama unemployment insurance is funded by employer contributions, not employee withholding. Alabama also exempts Social Security benefits from state income tax, and beginning in 2026 it allows a deduction for premium overtime pay under Act 2026-604, a break aimed at hourly workers.

    FAQ

    Does Alabama have a state income tax?

    Yes. Alabama taxes wage income on a graduated schedule with rates of 2%, 4%, and 5%, set in Code of Alabama 1975 § 40-18-5. The top rate of 5% applies to taxable income above $3,000 for a single filer and above $6,000 for a married couple filing jointly.

    What is the Alabama income tax rate for 2026?

    Alabama's rates for 2026 are 2% on the first $500 of taxable income, 4% on the next $2,500, and 5% on everything above $3,000 for a single filer, head of family, or married person filing separately. A married couple filing jointly pays 2% on the first $1,000, 4% on the next $5,000, and 5% above $6,000.

    Does Alabama have a standard deduction or personal exemption?

    Alabama grants a personal exemption of $1,500 for a single filer, a married person filing separately, or a head of family, and $3,000 for a married couple filing jointly, and it also allows a standard deduction that varies with income. The simplified 2026 data behind this calculator uses a $3,000 single-filer standard deduction instead, so treat the state line as an estimate.

    How much is taken out of a $55,000 salary in Alabama?

    For 2026, a single filer paid biweekly takes home about $1,722.21 per paycheck from a $55,000 salary: $2,115.38 gross, $170.00 federal income tax, $131.15 Social Security, $30.67 Medicare, and $61.35 Alabama state income tax. That is about $44,777.50 a year.

    Does Alabama have a local or city income tax?

    Alabama levies no county or statewide local income tax on wages. A few cities, including Birmingham, Montgomery, and Gadsden, charge a municipal occupational tax of about 1% or less under their own ordinances. This calculator does not model a city occupational tax, so a worker inside one of those city limits nets slightly less than the estimate shown.

    Does Alabama have disability or paid family leave withholding?

    No. Alabama has no state disability insurance program and no state paid family leave payroll tax, so neither is deducted from a paycheck. Alabama unemployment insurance is an employer-paid tax, not an employee deduction.

    Can Alabama taxpayers deduct the federal income tax they paid?

    Yes, and it is unusual. Alabama allows a taxpayer to deduct the federal income tax paid during the year, which lowers Alabama taxable income. This calculator does not subtract that federal deduction, so its Alabama line runs a little high; your employer's withholding tables account for it.

    Does Alabama tax overtime or retirement income?

    Beginning with tax year 2026, Alabama allows a deduction for premium overtime pay under Act 2026-604, which helps hourly workers. Alabama also exempts Social Security benefits from state income tax and offers a retirement income exclusion for some filers 65 and older. Those breaks apply to overtime or retirement income, not to the ordinary wages this calculator models.
